sentiment.rationale: The full-year 2025 guidance was meaningfully raised: underlying EBIT guidance was narrowed upward from $2.0-3.5bn to $3.0-3.5bn, and underlying EBITDA guidance was raised from $8.0-9.5bn to $9.0-9.5bn. The improvement is organic, driven by strong volume performance, Gemini cooperation cost savings, and operational efficiencies across all segments, not attributed to one-time items or FX. Management expressed confidence in sustained demand and the ability to continue delivering operational improvements.

summary.revenue: Q3 2025 revenue was USD 14,206 million, down 9.9% year-on-year from USD 15,762 million.
summary.eps: Q3 2025 earnings per share were USD 69, down from USD 193 in Q3 2024.
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025 guidance refined: underlying EBITDA raised to USD 9.0-9.5bn (from 8.0-9.5bn), underlying EBIT raised to USD 3.0-3.5bn (from 2.0-3.5bn), free cash flow raised to USD 1.0bn or higher (from -1.0bn or higher). Global container market volume growth revised to around 4% (previously 2-4%).
summary.margin: Q3 2025 EBIT margin was 9.0%, up 2.6 percentage points sequentially from 6.4% in Q2 2025, but down from 21.0% in Q3 2024.
key_risks: Continued pressure on Ocean freight rates, which declined 31% year-on-year.
Ongoing uncertainty in the geopolitical environment, including the Red Sea disruption expected to last for the full year.
Trade imbalances leading to higher empty container repositioning and handling costs.
The IMO Net Zero Framework delay, which marks a loss of momentum in global decarbonisation efforts.
Several terminals nearing optimal utilisation limit, potentially constraining volume growth.
key_opportunities: Gemini cooperation delivering cost savings above original target, with annualised benefits of USD 720-950m.
Strong volume growth in Ocean (7.0% year-on-year) and high utilisation of 94%.
Logistics & Services EBIT margin improving to 5.5% driven by operational improvements and cost control.
Terminals delivering record-high volumes, revenue, EBITDA, and EBIT with ROIC of 17.2%.
Strong demand out of China, with China's global export share increasing to about 37%.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management described the quarter as 'strong execution across all businesses' and expressed confidence in sustained demand, stating 'we do not expect this trend of accelerated export growth from China to stop' and that the guidance raise reflects 'confidence in sustained demand and operational improvements.'
